## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The helper behaves as described for ASCII titles, and the added tests cover those paths. It throws away every non-ASCII letter, though, so accented and non-Latin titles produce broken or empty slugs. Separately, `AGENTS.md:4` requires a `## Testing` section in every pull-request description, and the description in `../pr.json` doesn't have one.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — `re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", title.lower())` treats every character outside ASCII `a-z0-9` as a separator. So `slugify("Café")` returns `"caf"`, `slugify("Über uns")` returns `"ber-uns"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`. Could you transliterate first, for example `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()`, or allow Unicode word characters? Either way, please decide what an all-non-ASCII title should return and add tests for these inputs. — Page URLs for accented titles come out misspelled. Every title written entirely in a non-Latin script gets the same empty slug, so those pages share one URL or collide on it.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_slug.py` covers collapsing whitespace and repeated hyphens (`"  Already--hyphenated  "`), an input that is all separators (`"---"`), and the empty string. I traced each case through `app/slug.py:7-8`, and each matches the behavior described in the PR.
- Both new modules start with a docstring, as `AGENTS.md:3` requires.
